You are a careful, neutral coder of the REALIZED OUTCOME of a corporate transaction
over the 3-5 years AFTER it closed. You are given ONE evidence slice assembled from
public primary sources (financial filings, reputable press) that describes ONLY the
post-deal trajectory -- how the combined company actually fared. You are
DELIBERATELY NOT shown how the deal was structured at closing (what transferred and
what did not), and you must NOT speculate about the deal's structure. Code STRICTLY
the documented realized outcome. If the slice does not let you determine a field,
you MUST return "uncertain" -- never guess, never infer from outside knowledge.

Emit a single structured record with these fields.

C. FAILURE-PATHWAY INCIDENCE -- code strictly from the DOCUMENTED OUTCOME at the
3-5 year horizon. A pathway is a REALIZED DISRUPTION OVER TIME, not a structural
property of the deal.
  p4_pathway: Is there documented disruption specifically at the product/process
    interface (the acquired product could not be aligned with the operating
    processes over time; product-line/operations incoherence realized after the
    deal)? 1 = yes; 0 = no / none documented; uncertain.
  p5_pathway: Is there documented fracture specifically at the process/organization
    interface (operations vs people/management/culture; integration of operations
    broke against the organization over time)? 1 = yes; 0 = no / none documented;
    uncertain.
  t1_archetype: Is there documented incoherence in the controlling-intent archetype
    itself as it played out (e.g. an announced "merger of equals" that operated as
    one-sided dominance)? A channel SEPARATE from the product/process and
    process/organization pathways. 1 = yes; 0 = no; uncertain.
  t2_model: Is there documented incompatibility of the two business models
    (value-capture logics that could not be reconciled over time)? A channel
    SEPARATE from the pathways above. 1 = yes; 0 = no; uncertain.

D. performance_metric: the single best-documented post-deal outcome scalar in the
   slice (e.g. "divested 80.1% after ~108 months", "~$99bn goodwill write-down",
   "no divestiture; assets retained"). One short phrase. If none, "not documented".

p5_pathway codes specifically. Cite ONLY realized-outcome evidence; do NOT reason
about how the deal was structured at closing.

Emit ONLY the structured record. Code conservatively: absence of documented
evidence for a pathway is 0 (not-documented); inability to determine is "uncertain".

# Outcome sub-dossier — Motorola Mobility realized record after separation, ~3–5-year horizon (~2013–2015)

> EVIDENTIARY STANDARD: every factual line ends with a `[SRC: <SEC accession / URL>]`
> tag pointing to a public primary source. A fact that cannot be so sourced is written
> `[UNVERIFIED]` and is never guessed. The outcome window fixed at construction is the
> ~2013–2015 realized record of the separated Motorola Mobility business. Because the
> entity was acquired whole and deregistered before that window opened, there is no
> standalone public audited record within it; the traceable record is limited to the
> whole-entity acquisition and the subsequent product-business divestiture. This
> sub-dossier contains no information about how the original separation was structured.

## Public-reporting status after the separation (feasibility-relevant)
- The registrant filed only two annual reports on Form 10-K after separation: for fiscal
  2010 (filed 2011-02-18) and fiscal 2011 (filed 2012-02-17); no Form 10-K or 20-F was
  filed thereafter. [SRC: SEC accession 0001193125-11-040013, Form 10-K] [SRC: SEC accession 0001193125-12-067566, Form 10-K]
- The registrant filed a Form 15 (Rule 12g-4(a)(1) / 12h-3(b)(1)(i)) on June 1, 2012 to
  terminate registration and suspend its reporting duty; the number of holders of record as
  of the notice date was 1. [SRC: SEC accession 0001193125-12-256913, Form 15-12B]
- Consequently no separate audited public financial statements exist for the ~2013–2015
  outcome window, and the realized-record facts below rely on the whole-entity acquisition
  filing, the deregistration filing, and a within-window divestiture filing rather than on
  a standalone annual report. [SRC: SEC accession 0001193125-12-256913, Form 15-12B]

## Realized disposition of the separated entity (best-documented scalar)
- On May 22, 2012, Google Inc. completed the acquisition of Motorola Mobility: Merger Sub
  merged into Motorola Mobility, which became a wholly owned subsidiary of Google; each
  outstanding common share (with customary exceptions) was cancelled and converted into the
  right to receive $40.00 in cash, for a total purchase price of approximately
  $12.9 billion, financed with cash on hand. [SRC: SEC accession 0000903423-12-000298, Form 8-K]
- In connection with the closing, the common shares were delisted: on May 22, 2012 the NYSE
  filed a Form 25 to remove the shares from listing, and the registrant stated it would file
  a Form 15 to deregister and suspend reporting. [SRC: SEC accession 0000903423-12-000298, Form 8-K]

## Documented change at the organization/management interface at absorption
- Upon the merger, the entire pre-existing board resigned (including Dr. Sanjay K. Jha,
  Anthony J. Vinciquerra, Jon E. Barfield, Jeanne P. Jackson, Keith A. Meister, Daniel A.
  Ninivaggi, Thomas J. Meredith, James R. Stengel, and Dr. Andrew J. Viterbi), and the
  Merger Sub directors (Donald Harrison, Patrick Pichette, Kent Walker) became the
  directors. [SRC: SEC accession 0000903423-12-000298, Form 8-K]
- Immediately following the effective time, Dennis Woodside was appointed CEO, President and
  Secretary and Vanessa Wittman was appointed CFO and Treasurer — i.e., the senior
  management that had run the business was replaced by acquirer-installed leadership.
  [SRC: SEC accession 0000903423-12-000298, Form 8-K]

## Within-window product-business divestiture (~2014)
- On January 29, 2014, Google Inc. entered an Acquisition Agreement with Lenovo Group
  Limited to sell Google's Motorola Mobility mobile-devices business, including certain
  related assets, IP rights and contracts, for total consideration of $660 million in cash,
  $750 million in Lenovo ordinary shares, and a $1.5 billion promissory note payable at the
  third anniversary of closing; Google retained the vast majority of the patent portfolio,
  licensed back to the business for its continued operations. [SRC: SEC accession 0001288776-14-000008, Form 8-K (Google Inc.)]
- On October 30, 2014, Lenovo announced it had completed the acquisition of Motorola
  Mobility from Google for a total purchase price of approximately US$2.91 billion at close
  (approximately US$660 million in cash and 519,107,215 newly issued Lenovo shares valued at
  approximately US$750 million), adding a company with nearly 3,500 employees.
  [SRC: https://news.lenovo.com/pressroom/press-releases/lenovo-completes-full-acquisition-motorola-mobility-from-google/]

## Outcome summary (realized record only)
- The separated Motorola Mobility business generated no standalone public audited outcome
  record within the fixed ~2013–2015 window: it was acquired whole by Google (closed
  May 22, 2012; ~$12.9 billion; $40.00/share cash) and deregistered via Form 15 on
  June 1, 2012, before that window opened, and its senior management and board were
  replaced by the acquirer at absorption; the only documented within-window event affecting
  the business is Google's 2014 divestiture of the mobile-devices business to Lenovo (agreed
  January 29, 2014; completed October 30, 2014) with the patent portfolio retained by
  Google. The outcome for the separated entity across the window is therefore coded
  **uncertain** (no standalone public audited record). [SRC: SEC accession 0000903423-12-000298, Form 8-K] [SRC: SEC accession 0001193125-12-256913, Form 15-12B] [SRC: SEC accession 0001288776-14-000008, Form 8-K (Google Inc.)]

[SLICE END]
